1e4a89201a.q: What caused Apollo Ono's major real estate investment loss in 2006-2008 and how did he recover?
1e4a89201a.a: Apollo Ono invested in real estate through a fund between 2006 and 2008, writing promissory notes and loans, but the group committed mortgage fraud, including doctoring documents and falsifying information. He discovered this when a contact in Utah informed him that both principals had filed for personal bankruptcy without listing him as a creditor. He overcame this by radically owning the mistake rather than blaming the operators, then used that hard life lesson to compound his next generational move in real estate.

1c85a18430.a: Apollo Ono states that 80% of the Olympic athletes he knows from his cohort that have since retired and gone on to be successful are in real estate today, either in development, commercial real estate brokerage, residential real estate, or real estate development companies.

f4c74d2ec2.q: What is the General Adaptation Syndrome principle Apollo Ono applies to entrepreneurship from athletic training?
f4c74d2ec2.a: Apollo Ono describes the GAS principle—General Adaptation Syndrome—as alarm, resistance, then exhaustion. Growth happens when you recover a little bit before complete exhaustion. Unlike training 100% every day, athletes use periodization with large blocks of training volume followed by large blocks of recovery. Many entrepreneurs run never-ending block cycles until their decision-making quality falls apart, but this principle teaches that refreshed minds prevent burnout and sustain better performance.

2f0f6736c9.q: Why does Apollo Ono advocate for patience as a key attribute in both short track speed skating and real estate?
2f0f6736c9.a: Apollo Ono states that patience is a key attribute toward a sport like short track speed skating and the same thing applies in real estate. Performance is cyclical, not linear—you move forward, fail, revert back, learn, and begin again in small circles building momentum. Understanding that performance cycles up and down helps entrepreneurs resist the urge to overtrade, exit positions prematurely, or make reactive decisions, instead allowing them to be patient and persist through cycles.

bf8d084d3d.q: Why are mortgage rates hovering above 7% in September 2026 and will they come down?
bf8d084d3d.a: Mortgage rates are at approximately 7.2% as of mid-September 2026, the highest in over a year, driven primarily by rising Treasury yields. The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield is around 5%, the highest in quite a while, caused mainly by inflation from the war in Iran creating energy shocks, tariffs, and national deficit concerns. Dave Meyer does not expect rates to come down anytime soon because inflation has no clear path to improvement; his outlook is that rates will stay near 7% through the end of 2026, with a best-case scenario of the high sixes, but unlikely to fall below 6.75%.
bf8d084d3d.e: The Correction Will Get Even More Severe | Sept. 2026 Housing Market Update

695ecc22db.q: What is driving the increase in home inventory in the U.S. housing market in 2026?
695ecc22db.a: As of August 2026, according to Redfin, the total amount of homes for sale was 1.53 million, up 4% from July—an unusually large month-to-month change. This surge in supply is significant because higher mortgage rates have reduced demand, but instead of sitting out the market, sellers are now choosing to sell. This divergence between rising supply and falling demand creates a buyers market where sellers must compete by lowering prices.

ef3560b8eb.q: Which U.S. metro areas are experiencing the largest housing price declines in 2026?

8fc72e2baa.q: What is the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield in September 2026 and why does it matter for mortgage rates?
8fc72e2baa.a: The yield on a 10-year U.S. Treasury is approximately 5%—the highest it has been in quite a while—while 30-year treasuries are at their highest point in 30 years. Mortgage rates are directly tied to the yield on a 10-year U.S. Treasury, not what the Federal Reserve does; the higher Treasury yields directly drive higher mortgage rates across the economy.

1ad63fbb31.q: What investment strategy should real estate investors use in a declining housing market with rising inventory?
1ad63fbb31.a: Investors should focus on buying at significant discounts—aiming for 5% to 10% or 15% under current market comps—and seek out motivated sellers willing to lower prices and offer concessions. Dave Meyer advises identifying properties in great locations you would be happy to own 10 years from now, negotiating great prices, and being patient rather than rushing; there will be plenty of opportunities in the next couple of years as the percentage of motivated sellers cutting prices increases in a declining market.
